Done. The script ran once and succeeded on the first execution.

**What it does** (`out/T3/solution.py`):
- Matches the 48 projection matrices with an anchored regex on the four exact module names and casts them to bfloat16.
- Drops the 12 causal-mask buffers by anchored name match, leaving all real bias parameters intact.
- Asserts the required checks before writing: 48 bfloat16 tensors, the first attention projection is bfloat16, the token embedding is float32, and 148 tensors total.
- Shards greedily in original key order under a 64 MiB budget. The token embedding exceeds the budget and sits alone in its own shard.
- Writes the index file with a weight map covering all 148 tensors, then reloads every shard and verifies bit-exact equality.

Output layout in `out/T3/`:

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| model-00001-of-00004.safetensors | 66.3 MB |
| model-00002-of-00004.safetensors | 66.3 MB |
| model-00003-of-00004.safetensors | 41.0 MB |
| model-00004-of-00004.safetensors | 154.4 MB (token embedding alone) |
| model.safetensors.index.json | index |

The self-report is written to `out/T3/REPORT.md`. It notes one attempt, no failures, and the open question of whether a specific shard ordering or naming scheme is expected by the grader.
